newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE futures volume up 7.8 pct in June 1997 vs 1996.
newsitem.headline: WCE futures volume up 7.8 pct in June 1997 vs 1996.

text.p: Volume of trade rose 7.8 percent in futures contracts last month at the Winnipeg Commodity Exchange compared with June 1996, WCE figures show.
Canola, the WCE's most actively-traded futures contract, saw an 11.8 percent rise in volume as 116,117 contracts changed hands and a 16.8 percent rise since the start of the year August 1.
Trade in all futures contracts was up 7.8 percent with 159,243 contracts trading in June compared to 147,702 in the same month in 1996, the WCE said in a statement.
Western barley volume fell 17.7 percent with 18,912 contracts traded in June versus 22,968 in June 1996.
Feed wheat futures volume rose 19.1 percent as 13,738 contracts traded in June compared to 11,539 in June 1996.
Feed pea futures, the world's first such contract launched November 1, 1995, saw a 56.6 percent rise in volume with 2,045 contracts trading versus 1,306 in June 1996.
Flax futures, however, fell 1.8 percent to 7,851 contracts traded compared to 7,997 in June 1996.
Oats saw 580 contracts change hands in June 1997 compared to none in June 1996.
